items.q: What is the capital city of Vietnam?
items.h: Hà Nội is more than 1,000 years old and has lots of lakes.

items.q: What does 'xin chào' mean?
items.h: Xin chào is the friendly way to say hello in Vietnamese.

items.q: What does 'cảm ơn' mean?
items.h: Cảm ơn means thank you. Polite children say it to everyone!

items.q: What does 'tạm biệt' mean?
items.h: Tạm biệt means goodbye. Wave and say it when you leave a friend's house.

items.q: Phở is a Vietnamese soup made with which noodles?
items.h: Phở has flat rice noodles in a hot broth with herbs and beef or chicken.

items.q: Bánh mì is a crunchy Vietnamese what?
items.h: Bánh mì means bread. The crispy rolls are filled with meat, pickles and herbs.

items.q: What is the Vietnamese Lunar New Year called?
items.h: At Tết, families clean their homes, visit relatives and share bánh chưng.

items.q: What colour are the lucky money envelopes given at Tết?
items.h: Lì xì envelopes are red, a lucky colour, and hold new banknotes for children.

items.q: What is bánh chưng, the square Tết cake, wrapped in?
items.h: Bánh chưng is sticky rice wrapped in green dong leaves, then boiled for many hours.

items.q: What do children carry at the Mid-Autumn Festival?
items.h: At Trung Thu, children parade with star-shaped lanterns under the full moon.

items.q: Which cake is eaten at the Mid-Autumn Festival?
items.h: Mooncakes are round like the full moon and filled with beans, seeds or egg yolk.

items.q: What shape is the Vietnamese hat called nón lá?
items.h: The nón lá is a cone-shaped hat that keeps off both sun and rain.

items.q: What is the nón lá hat made from?
items.h: Nón lá means leaf hat. Palm leaves are sewn onto thin bamboo rings.

items.q: Which big animal helps farmers plough Vietnam's rice fields?
items.h: Water buffaloes pull ploughs through mud and love to cool off in ponds.

items.q: Which flower grows in muddy ponds and is loved in Vietnam?
items.h: The lotus grows out of mud but opens clean pink or white flowers.

items.q: Hạ Long Bay is famous for its many what?
items.h: Hạ Long Bay has more than 1,600 limestone islands in green water.

items.q: Which animal is in the name of Hạ Long Bay?
items.h: Hạ Long means descending dragon. A legend says a dragon made the islands.

items.q: Which country is Vietnam's neighbour to the north?
items.h: Vietnam's neighbours are China to the north, and Laos and Cambodia to the west.

items.q: What is the main colour of Vietnam's flag?
items.h: Vietnam's flag is red with a big five-pointed yellow star in the middle.

items.q: The map of Vietnam looks like which letter?
items.h: Vietnam is long and thin and curves like the letter S beside the sea.

items.q: Which city was the royal capital of Vietnam's last emperors?
items.h: Huế's old citadel still has palaces, gates, thick walls and a moat.

items.q: Hội An's old town is famous for its colourful what?
items.h: Hội An's streets are hung with silk lanterns that glow in many colours at night.

items.q: Which cool hill city in Vietnam is famous for flowers?
items.h: Đà Lạt is cool all year, so farmers grow flowers and strawberries there.

items.q: Which big river flows into the sea in southern Vietnam?
items.h: The Mekong flows through six countries before it reaches the sea in Vietnam.

items.q: Where are Vietnam's famous floating markets?
items.h: In the Mekong Delta, people buy and sell fruit from boats on the river.

items.q: Which mountain town in Vietnam has rice terraces like giant steps?
items.h: Sa Pa sits high in misty mountains near Fansipan, Vietnam's top peak.

items.q: Which little orange fruit tree do families buy for Tết?
items.h: Kumquat trees covered in little orange fruits are a sign of good luck at Tết.

items.q: Vietnamese water puppets put on their show on what?
items.h: Water puppets began in rice fields. Puppeteers stand in water behind a screen.

items.q: Which long Vietnamese outfit is worn over trousers?
items.h: Áo dài means long shirt. People wear it for Tết, weddings and school.

items.q: What does 'mẹ' mean in English?
items.h: Mẹ means mum and bố means dad, just like in this family of fighters!

items.q: In 'trà đá', what does 'đá' mean?
items.h: Trà đá is iced tea, a favourite street drink. Trà means tea and đá means ice.

items.q: What does 'nước' mean in English?
items.h: Nước means water. Nước mía is a sweet juice made from sugar cane.

items.q: Which fruit, grown in Vietnam, comes from a cactus?
items.h: Dragon fruit has pink skin with green tips. Inside are tiny black seeds.

items.q: Which pink blossom fills homes in northern Vietnam at Tết?
items.h: In the north, homes have pink peach blossom at Tết; in the south, yellow mai.

items.q: In đá cầu, players keep a shuttlecock up with what?
items.h: Đá cầu means kick the shuttlecock. Players may use anything but their hands.

items.q: Phong Nha in Vietnam is famous for its giant what?
items.h: Sơn Đoòng cave in Phong Nha is so big it has its own jungle and clouds inside!

items.q: Which lake in Hà Nội has a legend about a golden turtle?
items.h: In the legend, a golden turtle takes back a magic sword from the king.

items.q: What is Vietnam's money called?
items.h: Vietnam uses the đồng. Japan uses the yen, and the USA uses the dollar.

items.q: What are chả giò, or nem rán?
items.h: Chả giò (south) and nem rán (north) are crispy fried rolls filled with meat.

items.q: Which pancake is named after the sizzle it makes in the pan?
items.h: Xèo is the sizzling sound of the batter. Turmeric makes the pancake yellow.

items.q: Bến Tre in the Mekong Delta is famous for which tree?
items.h: Bến Tre is the land of coconuts. People make sweets, rope and mats from them.

items.q: What does 'con mèo' mean?
items.h: Con mèo is a cat and con chó is a dog. Mèo even sounds like meow!

items.q: Which animal is in Vietnam's zodiac instead of the Rabbit?
items.h: China's zodiac has a Rabbit, but Vietnam's has a Cat. Both have 12 animals.

items.q: What does 'cơm' mean in Vietnamese?
items.h: 'Ăn cơm chưa?' means 'Have you eaten?' and is a friendly way to say hi.

items.q: Which tall, fast-growing plant was used to build Vietnamese homes?
items.h: Bamboo is a giant grass. It makes houses, baskets, bridges and chopsticks.

items.q: Which river flows through Hà Nội?
items.h: The Red River is named after its reddish-brown, muddy water.

items.q: What is Mũi Né in Vietnam famous for?
items.h: Mũi Né has big red and white sand dunes, and children slide down them on boards.

items.q: What does 'Chúc mừng năm mới' mean?
items.h: People say Chúc mừng năm mới at Tết. Năm mới means new year.

items.q: Vietnamese is written with the same ABC letters as which language?
items.h: Vietnamese uses ABC letters plus little marks that show how each word sounds.

items.q: Which rare animal of Vietnam's forests is called the Asian unicorn?
items.h: Scientists first found the shy saola in 1992. It has two long, straight horns.

items.q: In which months does Tết come?
items.h: Tết follows the Moon, so its date moves each year, from late January to February.

items.q: Which Vietnamese instrument has just one string?
items.h: The đàn bầu has only one string, yet it can sing many notes, like a voice.

items.q: Vietnam's ancient Đông Sơn drums are made of what?
items.h: Đông Sơn drums are over 2,000 years old, with a star and flying birds on top.

items.q: Which fruit's Vietnamese name, chôm chôm, means messy hair?
items.h: Rambutans have hairy red skin. Peel it to find sweet white fruit inside.

items.q: Which bridge in Đà Nẵng breathes fire and water?
items.h: On weekend nights, Đà Nẵng's Dragon Bridge breathes fire and sprays water!

items.q: Which is the fastest land animal?
items.h: Cheetahs can reach about 100 kilometres an hour, but only in short dashes.

items.q: Which is the biggest animal on Earth?
items.h: A blue whale is longer than two buses, and its tongue weighs as much as an elephant!

items.q: What is a baby cat called?
items.h: Kittens are born with their eyes shut and open them at one to two weeks old.

items.q: What is a baby sheep called?
items.h: Lambs can stand up and walk soon after they are born.

items.q: What is a baby horse called?
items.h: A foal can stand up and wobble about within a couple of hours of being born.

items.q: What does a tadpole grow into?
items.h: A tadpole lives in water and has a tail. Later it grows legs and loses the tail.

items.q: Where does a baby kangaroo grow after it is born?
items.h: A newborn joey is as small as a jelly bean and grows in its mum's pouch.

items.q: What does a caterpillar turn into?
items.h: Inside a hard case called a chrysalis, a caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

items.q: How many legs does a spider have?
items.h: Spiders have 8 legs. Insects, like ants and bees, have 6.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.h: Insects like ants have 6 legs and a body made of 3 parts.

items.q: Which big cat lives in groups called prides?
items.h: In a pride of lions, the lionesses do most of the hunting together.

items.q: Which animal has a long trunk?
items.h: An elephant uses its trunk to smell, drink, lift things and say hello.

items.q: Which animal has the longest neck?
items.h: A giraffe's neck has 7 bones, the same number as yours, but each one is huge!

items.q: Which bird cannot fly but swims very well?
items.h: Penguins use their wings like flippers to zoom through the water.

items.q: What is the biggest bird?
items.h: Ostriches cannot fly, but they run fast and lay the biggest eggs of any living bird.

items.q: Which animal carries its home on its back?
items.h: A snail's shell grows with it, and it can hide inside to stay safe and damp.

items.q: Which insect makes honey?
items.h: Honeybees make honey from flower nectar and keep it in little wax cells.

items.q: Where do honeybees live?
items.h: A hive can hold tens of thousands of honeybees, but just one queen.

items.q: What is a fox's home called?
items.h: A fox's den, also called an earth, is often a hole dug underground.

items.q: What does a beaver use to cut down trees?
items.h: Beavers gnaw down trees to build dams. Their front teeth are orange from iron!

items.q: What do giant pandas mostly eat?
items.h: Giant pandas spend about half of every day munching bamboo.

items.q: Which sea animal is a mammal?
items.h: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole and feed their babies milk.

items.q: Which of these animals is a fish?
items.h: Sharks are fish that breathe with gills. Whales, dolphins and seals breathe air.

items.q: Which of these animals is an amphibian?
items.h: Amphibians like frogs start life in water and later live on land too.

items.q: Which animal sleeps through the winter?
items.h: Hedgehogs hibernate: they sleep all winter in a cosy nest of leaves.

items.q: What is a group of fish called?
items.h: Fish swim together in a school, or shoal, to stay safe.

items.q: What is a group of wolves called?
items.h: Wolves live and hunt in family groups called packs.

items.q: What colour is a polar bear's skin?
items.h: Under its white-looking fur, a polar bear has black skin to soak up the sun.

items.q: Which animal stores fat in its hump?
items.h: A camel's hump stores fat, not water, so it can go a long time without food.

items.q: Which animal is famous for changing its colour?
items.h: Chameleons change colour to show their mood, to warm up and to hide.

items.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
items.h: An octopus has 3 hearts and 8 arms, and it can squirt ink to escape.

items.q: Which animal has black and white stripes?
items.h: No two zebras have exactly the same stripes, just like your fingerprints.

items.q: Which animal eats only plants?
items.h: Rabbits are herbivores: they eat grass, leaves and vegetables, never meat.

items.q: Which bird can turn its head almost all the way round?
items.h: An owl can turn its head about three-quarters of the way round!

items.q: Which bird can fly backwards?
items.h: Hummingbirds flap their wings so fast that they hum, and they can fly backwards.

items.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
items.h: Gills take in oxygen from the water as it flows past them.

items.q: What is a male chicken called?
items.h: A cockerel crows in the morning, and a hen lays the eggs.

items.q: Which sea animal usually has five arms?
items.h: If a starfish loses an arm, it can grow a new one!

items.q: Which mammal lays eggs?
items.h: The platypus has a bill like a duck and lays eggs, yet it feeds its babies milk.

items.q: Which animal with a shell can live for over 100 years?
items.h: Giant tortoises are slow movers, but they can live for more than 100 years.

items.q: Which is the biggest kind of cat?
items.h: Tigers are the biggest cats, and every tiger has its own stripe pattern.

items.q: Which animal spins silk to make a cocoon?
items.h: A silkworm spins its cocoon from one very long thread of silk.

items.q: Which animal has a horn on its nose?
items.h: A rhino's horn is made of keratin, the same stuff as your hair and nails.

items.q: Which mammal can really fly?
items.h: Bats are the only mammals that can really fly. Their wings are made of skin.

items.q: What is an animal that eats only meat called?
items.h: Carnivores like lions eat meat; herbivores like cows eat plants.

items.q: What do all baby mammals drink?
items.h: From mice to whales, every baby mammal drinks its mother's milk.

items.q: Which bird is pink because of the food it eats?
items.h: Flamingos are pink because of the shrimps and tiny plants they eat.

items.q: Which bird opens a big fan of colourful tail feathers?
items.h: Only the males, called peacocks, have the big shimmering tail fans.

items.q: Which animal catches ants with its long sticky tongue?
items.h: An anteater can flick its tongue in and out about 150 times a minute!

items.q: Which animal hangs upside down and moves very slowly?
items.h: Sloths move so slowly that tiny green plants called algae grow in their fur.

items.q: Which is the biggest ocean?
items.h: The Pacific is so big that all the land on Earth could fit inside it.

items.q: Which of these is a continent?
items.h: Europe is a continent. France is one of the countries inside it.

items.q: Which continent is the coldest?
items.h: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth and is covered in thick ice.

items.q: Which is the biggest continent?
items.h: Asia is the biggest continent, and Vietnam is part of it.

items.q: Which continent is Kenya in?
items.h: Kenya, in East Africa, is famous for its wild lions, zebras and giraffes.

items.q: Which huge sandy desert is in northern Africa?
items.h: The Sahara is the biggest hot desert, almost as big as the whole USA.

items.q: What is the capital of the United Kingdom?
items.h: London is the UK's capital. Its famous bell, Big Ben, hangs in a clock tower.

items.q: What is the capital of Spain?
items.h: Madrid, the capital of Spain, is right in the middle of the country.

items.q: What is the capital of Germany?
items.h: Berlin is Germany's capital. Its Brandenburg Gate is more than 200 years old.

items.q: Which country is Mount Fuji in?
items.h: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain, a snowy volcano shaped like a cone.

items.q: In which country do wild kangaroos live?
items.h: Australia is a country and a continent, home of kangaroos and koalas.

items.q: Which ocean lies between Europe and America?
items.h: The Atlantic is the second biggest ocean. Ships cross it from Europe to America.

items.q: Which ocean is around the North Pole?
items.h: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest ocean, and much of it is covered in ice.

items.q: What do we call land with water all around it?
items.h: An island has water all around it. Great Britain is a big island.

items.q: What is the highest mountain in the world?
items.h: Mount Everest, between Nepal and China, is the highest mountain on Earth.

items.q: What colours are on Japan's flag?
items.h: Japan's flag is a red circle, the rising sun, on a white background.

items.q: Which country's flag has a red maple leaf?
items.h: Canada's flag has a red maple leaf. Maple syrup comes from maple trees.

items.q: Which continent is Brazil in?
items.h: Brazil is in South America and has much of the Amazon rainforest.

items.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
items.h: Maps usually put north at the top. A compass helps you find north.

items.q: Which country is famous for tulips and windmills?
items.h: The Netherlands is very flat, and some of its land is lower than the sea.

items.q: Which is the biggest country on Earth?
items.h: Russia is in both Europe and Asia, and it is much bigger than any other country.

items.q: What does a desert get very little of?
items.h: A desert gets very little rain. Icy Antarctica counts as a desert too!

items.q: The Amazon in South America is a huge river and a giant what?
items.h: The Amazon rainforest is home to jaguars, sloths, parrots and millions of insects.

items.q: Which country is home to the kiwi bird?
items.h: The kiwi cannot fly. People from New Zealand are nicknamed Kiwis too!

items.q: What is the capital of the USA?
items.h: Washington, D.C. is the US capital, but New York is a much bigger city.

items.q: Which ocean is named after a country?
items.h: The Indian Ocean is named after India, and it is the warmest ocean.

items.q: Which country of the UK has a red dragon on its flag?
items.h: The Welsh flag shows a red dragon on green and white.

items.q: What is the capital of Northern Ireland?
items.h: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, one of the four parts of the UK.

items.q: Which river flows through Paris?
items.h: The River Seine winds through Paris, right past the Eiffel Tower.

items.q: Which river flows through Egypt?
items.h: Ancient Egyptians farmed the rich, dark soil beside the River Nile.

items.q: Which season comes after winter?
items.h: In spring, days get longer, flowers open and many baby animals are born.

items.q: In which season do leaves turn red and gold?
items.h: In autumn, leaves turn red, orange and gold, then drop from the trees.

items.q: What colour are most leaves?
items.h: Leaves are green because of chlorophyll, which helps them make food from light.

items.q: Which tree grows from an acorn?
items.h: A tiny acorn can grow into a mighty oak tree that lives for hundreds of years.

items.q: What do you need to see a rainbow?
items.h: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through drops of rain.

items.q: Which balls of ice can drop from storm clouds?
items.h: Hailstones are balls of ice that grow bigger inside tall storm clouds.

items.q: Snowflakes are made of tiny crystals of what?
items.h: Snowflakes are ice crystals, and most have six sides or six points.

items.q: What do bees carry from flower to flower?
items.h: Bees carry pollen between flowers, which helps the plants make seeds.

items.q: Which part of a plant usually grows under the ground?
items.h: Roots hold a plant in the soil and drink up the water it needs.

items.q: What is a mountain that can erupt with lava called?
items.h: Melted rock is called magma inside a volcano and lava when it comes out.

items.q: What is a huge, slow river of ice called?
items.h: Glaciers move very slowly and carve out deep valleys as they go.

items.q: Young sunflowers turn to follow what?
items.h: Young sunflowers follow the Sun across the sky; grown-up ones face east.

items.q: Which tree has needles and stays green all year?
items.h: Pine trees are evergreen: they keep their needle-like leaves all year.

items.q: Which is the hottest season in Britain?
items.h: In summer the days are long, so the Sun has more time to warm the ground.

items.q: What are clouds mostly made of?
items.h: Clouds are billions of tiny water drops or ice bits floating in the air.

items.q: Which part of an apple can grow into a new tree?
items.h: Apple pips are seeds. Plant one and it may grow into a new apple tree.

items.q: Which soft white rock can you draw with?
items.h: Chalk is made of the shells of tiny sea plankton from millions of years ago.

items.q: Which part of a plant makes the seeds?
items.h: Flowers make seeds, and many seeds grow inside fruits.

items.q: Which desert plant stores water in its thick stem?
items.h: A cactus stores water in its stem, and its prickly spines are special leaves.

items.q: What makes the bang of thunder?
items.h: Lightning heats the air so fast that it bangs: that bang is thunder.

items.q: What white icy coating covers grass on cold mornings?
items.h: Frost forms when water in the air freezes onto cold grass and windows.

items.q: Chocolate is made from the beans of which tree?
items.h: Cocoa beans grow inside big pods on the cacao tree.

items.q: Which fruit is dried to make raisins?
items.h: Raisins are grapes that have been dried, often in the sun.

items.q: How many seasons are there in a year in Britain?
items.h: Britain has 4 seasons, but southern Vietnam has 2: a wet one and a dry one.

items.q: What can you count to tell how old a tree is?
items.h: Most trees grow one new ring every year inside their trunk.

items.q: What is moving air called?
items.h: Wind is moving air. It can spin windmills and lift kites high.

items.q: Which crop grows in watery fields called paddies?
items.h: Rice is the main food for more than half the people in the world.

items.q: Which spiky fruit is famous for its very strong smell?
items.h: Durian is called the king of fruits, but some hotels ban it because of its smell!

items.q: Which of these does a magnet pull?
items.h: Magnets pull things made of iron and steel, but not wood, plastic or glass.

items.q: At what temperature does water freeze?
items.h: Water freezes into ice at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C.

items.q: When water boils, what does it turn into?
items.h: Boiling water turns into a gas called steam, or water vapour.

items.q: Which of these is a solid?
items.h: Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow, and gases spread out to fill a space.

items.q: What do we use to measure how hot something is?
items.h: A thermometer shows how hot or cold something is, in degrees.

items.q: Which material can you see through?
items.h: Glass is made mostly from sand, melted at very high temperatures.

items.q: Which material is made from trees?
items.h: Paper is made from wood, so recycling paper helps to save trees.

items.q: Which material is bendy and stretchy?
items.h: Natural rubber comes from the milky sap of the rubber tree.

items.q: What do we call a push or a pull?
items.h: A force is a push or a pull. Kicking a ball is a push!

items.q: Which force pulls everything down to the ground?
items.h: Gravity pulls things down to the ground, and it keeps the Moon near Earth.

items.q: Which of these is the fastest?
items.h: Light is the fastest thing there is. Sunlight reaches Earth in about 8 minutes.

items.q: Sounds are made when things do what?
items.h: Sounds come from things shaking very fast, like a drum skin when you hit it.

items.q: What forms when something blocks the light?
items.h: Shadows are long in the morning and evening, and short in the middle of the day.

items.q: What is a sound that bounces back to you called?
items.h: Shout in a cave or a big empty hall and the sound bounces back as an echo.

items.q: What do you see when you look in a mirror?
items.h: A mirror bounces light back, so you see your reflection the wrong way round.

items.q: What does a battery store and give out?
items.h: A battery stores energy and gives it out as electricity for toys and torches.

items.q: Which of these floats on water?
items.h: Cork floats because it is very light for its size and full of tiny air pockets.

items.q: Which of these melts when it gets warm?
items.h: Chocolate melts at about the heat of your body, so it melts in your mouth!

items.q: Which gas do plants give out that we need to breathe?
items.h: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen, which we breathe in.

items.q: Which force slows down a ball rolling on grass?
items.h: Friction is a force that slows things down when they rub together.

items.q: Rub a balloon on your hair. What makes it stick to a wall?
items.h: Rubbing makes static electricity, which can make balloons stick and hair stand up.

items.q: Which of these makes its own light?
items.h: The Moon makes no light of its own; it shines because sunlight bounces off it.

items.q: Which metal goes rusty when it gets wet?
items.h: Iron rusts when water and air touch it, turning it flaky and orange-brown.

items.q: How many colours do we name in a rainbow?
items.h: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet: 7 rainbow colours.

items.q: Which colour is between red and yellow in a rainbow?
items.h: Rainbow colours always sit in the same order, with orange between red and yellow.

items.q: The Sun is a giant ball of what?
items.h: The Sun is a star, a giant ball of hot, glowing gas. It is our closest star.

items.q: How many planets go around our Sun?
items.h: The 8 planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

items.q: Which planet do we live on?
items.h: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, and the only one known to have life.

items.q: Which is the biggest planet?
items.h: Jupiter is so big that more than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.

items.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
items.h: Mars looks red because its dusty ground is full of rust.

items.q: Which planet has big, bright rings?
items.h: Saturn's rings are made of billions of chunks of ice and rock.

items.q: Which is the smallest planet?
items.h: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest one to the Sun.

items.q: Which is the hottest planet?
items.h: Venus is even hotter than Mercury because its thick clouds trap the heat.

items.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
items.h: Neptune is a cold, windy blue planet, the farthest of the 8 from the Sun.

items.q: What does the Moon travel around?
items.h: The Moon goes all the way around the Earth about once a month.

items.q: How long does Earth take to go once around the Sun?
items.h: Earth takes one year, about 365 days, to travel once around the Sun.

items.q: When your side of Earth faces away from the Sun, what time is it?
items.h: Earth spins round once a day, carrying you into sunlight and then into darkness.

items.q: What did Neil Armstrong walk on in 1969?
items.h: Neil Armstrong was the first person on the Moon, and Buzz Aldrin came next.

items.q: What carries astronauts up into space?
items.h: Rockets blast off by pushing out hot gas. Yuri Gagarin rode one into space in 1961.

items.q: What do we call a person trained to travel into space?
items.h: In space stations, astronauts float, so they sleep in sleeping bags tied to walls.

items.q: What are the round holes on the Moon called?
items.h: Craters were made when space rocks crashed into the Moon long ago.

items.q: What do we call a group of stars that makes a picture?
items.h: Constellations are star patterns, like the Great Bear or Orion the Hunter.

items.q: What is a huge group of billions of stars called?
items.h: We live in a galaxy called the Milky Way. On dark nights it looks like a misty band.

items.q: A shooting star is really a bit of what?
items.h: Shooting stars are bits of space rock or dust glowing as they zoom into our air.

items.q: Which planet spins on its side?
items.h: Uranus is tipped right over, so it rolls around the Sun like a ball.

items.q: What is a thin, curved Moon shape called?
items.h: The Moon seems to change shape as we see different parts of it lit by the Sun.

items.q: How many moons does Earth have?
items.h: Earth has one Moon. Mars has two tiny moons, and Jupiter has lots.

items.q: What do astronauts wear to go outside a spacecraft?
items.h: A spacesuit gives astronauts air to breathe and keeps them warm and safe.

items.q: What is a ball of ice and dust with a glowing tail?
items.h: When a comet comes near the Sun, its ice warms up and makes a long glowing tail.

items.q: In which direction does the Sun rise?
items.h: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west because the Earth spins.

items.q: How many senses do we usually learn about?
items.h: The 5 senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

items.q: Which part of your body do you smell with?
items.h: Your nose can tell apart thousands of different smells.

items.q: Which part of your body do you hear with?
items.h: Your ears help you hear, and deep inside they also help you keep your balance!

items.q: Which part of your body do you taste with?
items.h: Your tongue is covered in thousands of tiny taste buds.

items.q: How many baby teeth do children have?
items.h: Children have 20 baby teeth, which make way for bigger grown-up teeth later.

items.q: Which part of your body beats inside your chest?
items.h: Your heart is a strong muscle about the size of your fist.

items.q: Which part of your body do you think with?
items.h: Your brain controls your whole body, even while you are asleep.

items.q: Which body parts fill up with air when you breathe in?
items.h: You have two lungs. They take oxygen from the air you breathe.

items.q: What is the frame of bones inside your body called?
items.h: A grown-up's skeleton has 206 bones.

items.q: Where in your body is your longest bone?
items.h: The thigh bone, or femur, is the longest and strongest bone in your body.

items.q: What makes your heart and lungs stronger?
items.h: Running, swimming and playing make your heart and lungs work hard and grow strong.

items.q: Which bone protects your brain like a helmet?
items.h: Your skull is a strong case of bone that keeps your brain safe.

items.q: What is the long line of bones down your back called?
items.h: Your spine is a stack of small bones that lets you bend, twist and stand tall.

items.q: What pulls on your bones to make you move?
items.h: Muscles pull on bones to move you. You have more than 600 of them!

items.q: What is the biggest organ of your body?
items.h: Your skin is your biggest organ. It keeps germs out and lets you feel touch.

items.q: What is the black dot in the middle of your eye called?
items.h: Your pupil is a hole that lets light in. It gets bigger in the dark.

items.q: Which of these is the healthiest snack?
items.h: Fruit like apples gives you vitamins and fibre, and it is naturally sweet.

items.q: How often should you brush your teeth?
items.h: Brush your teeth twice a day for two minutes to keep them strong.

items.q: Which sense do you use your eyes for?
items.h: Your eyes see colours and shapes, and blinking keeps them clean and wet.

items.q: Where does food go after you swallow it?
items.h: Your stomach squeezes and mashes food with special juices to break it down.

items.q: How many toes do most people have?
items.h: Most people have 10 toes. Your big toes help you balance when you walk.

items.q: Which joint lets your leg bend in the middle?
items.h: Your knee lets your leg bend, and a small bone called the kneecap protects it.

items.q: Whose fingerprints are exactly the same as yours?
items.h: Everybody's fingerprints are different. Even twins have different ones!

items.q: What is the hardest stuff in your body?
items.h: Tooth enamel, the shiny outside of your teeth, is even harder than bone.

items.q: Which country does pizza come from?
items.h: Pizza comes from Naples in Italy. A Margherita has the colours of Italy's flag.

items.q: Which country does sushi come from?
items.h: Sushi is from Japan. It is made with rice, often with fish or vegetables.

items.q: Which instrument has black and white keys?
items.h: A piano has 88 keys: 52 white ones and 36 black ones.

items.q: How many strings does a violin have?
items.h: A violin has 4 strings, and you play it by pulling a bow across them.

items.q: Which instrument do you play by hitting it with sticks?
items.h: Drums are some of the oldest instruments. People have played them for ages!

items.q: Which sport uses rackets and a feathered shuttlecock?
items.h: A badminton shuttlecock is made with 16 feathers fixed into a round cork.

items.q: How many players are in a football team on the pitch?
items.h: A football team has 11 players on the pitch, and one of them is the goalkeeper.

items.q: Which sport is played with a bat, a ball and wickets?
items.h: In cricket, the bowler tries to hit the wicket, and the batter guards it.

items.q: How often are the Summer Olympic Games held?
items.h: The Summer Olympics come every 4 years. The Winter Olympics are 2 years after.

items.q: Which language do people speak in Spain?
items.h: Spanish is spoken in Spain and in many countries of South America.

items.q: How do people say hello in France?
items.h: Bonjour means good day in French. In Spanish, people say hola.

items.q: Which country do tacos come from?
items.h: Tacos come from Mexico. They are tortillas folded around tasty fillings.

items.q: Which famous painting shows a smiling woman?
items.h: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa. It hangs in the Louvre in Paris.

items.q: Who painted the famous Sunflowers pictures?
items.h: Vincent van Gogh painted bright sunflowers with thick, swirly paint.

items.q: Which colour do you get by mixing blue and yellow paint?
items.h: Blue and yellow make green, and red and yellow make orange.

items.q: In Japan, families picnic under which pink blossom in spring?
items.h: Hanami means flower viewing: families picnic under cherry trees in spring.

items.q: Which country holds a giant carnival in Rio de Janeiro?
items.h: Rio's carnival has samba dancers in sparkly costumes on giant floats.

items.q: Origami is the Japanese art of folding what?
items.h: With origami, you can fold a paper crane from one square sheet.

items.q: Which instrument do you blow into?
items.h: You blow across a hole in a flute, and your fingers change the notes.

items.q: Which dance with stamping and clapping comes from Spain?
items.h: Flamenco dancers stamp, clap and twirl to Spanish guitar music.

items.q: Ballet dancers can dance on the tips of their what?
items.h: Ballet dancers wear special pointe shoes to dance on the tips of their toes.

items.q: Which game has kings, queens and knights?
items.h: In chess, the knight moves in an L shape, and the queen is the strongest piece.

items.q: Which language do most people speak in Brazil?
items.h: Brazil is the only country in South America where Portuguese is the main language.

items.q: Which sport do you play by throwing a ball through a hoop?
items.h: Basketball players bounce the ball as they run, and score through a high hoop.

items.q: What do people in Japan and Vietnam use to eat noodles?
items.h: Chopsticks are a pair of thin sticks. In Vietnamese, they are called đũa.

items.q: Which country built the Great Wall?
items.h: The Great Wall of China is thousands of kilometres long and over 2,000 years old.

items.q: In which country are the Great Pyramids of Giza?
items.h: The Great Pyramid is over 4,500 years old and is built from over 2 million stone blocks.

items.q: Which city is the Eiffel Tower in?
items.h: The Eiffel Tower was built from iron in 1889. It gets a new coat of paint every 7 years.

items.q: The Wright brothers built and flew the first what?
items.h: In 1903, the Wright brothers' first flight lasted just 12 seconds.

items.q: What is ancient Egyptian picture writing called?
items.h: Hieroglyphs used little pictures, like birds and eyes, as letters and words.

items.q: What did the Romans build to carry water into towns?
items.h: Some Roman aqueducts crossed valleys on tall stone bridges with many arches.

items.q: Which white marble building is a famous wonder in India?
items.h: The Taj Mahal's white marble seems to change colour from pink to gold in the light.

items.q: Which invention lets you talk to someone far away?
items.h: The first telephones were made about 150 years ago, and they had no screens.

items.q: Which very old invention helps carts and bikes roll?
items.h: The wheel was invented over 5,000 years ago. At first it helped people make pots!

items.q: Which invention from ancient China helps you find north?
items.h: The first Chinese compasses used a magnetic spoon that turned on a smooth plate.

items.q: Which ancient stone circle is in England?
items.h: Stonehenge is about 5,000 years old, and some of its stones came from Wales!

items.q: In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay first climbed what?
items.h: Hillary and Tenzing stood on top of the world's highest mountain on 29 May 1953.

items.q: The first Olympic Games were held in which country?
items.h: The first Olympic Games were held in ancient Greece nearly 3,000 years ago.

items.q: New York's big statue with a torch was a gift from which country?
items.h: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper, which slowly turned green over time.

items.q: Braille is a way of reading with your what?
items.h: Louis Braille invented his alphabet of raised dots when he was a teenager.

items.q: Which old clock uses the Sun's shadow to tell the time?
items.h: A sundial's shadow moves round as the Sun crosses the sky, showing the time.

items.q: How many days are there in a week?
items.h: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday: 7 days.

items.q: How many months are there in a year?
items.h: A year has 12 months, from January to December.

items.q: How many days are there in a year that is not a leap year?
items.h: A year has 365 days. A leap year, which comes about every 4 years, has 366.

items.q: How many minutes are there in an hour?
items.h: An hour has 60 minutes, and a minute has 60 seconds.

items.q: How many hours are there in a day?
items.h: A day has 24 hours, so the short hand of a clock goes round twice.

items.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
items.h: Tri means three: a triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

items.q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
items.h: Penta means five, so a pentagon has 5 sides and 5 corners.

items.q: What 3D shape is a football?
items.h: A sphere is round all over, like a ball, a marble or a bubble.

items.q: What 3D shape is a dice?
items.h: A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

items.q: What is half of 10?
items.h: Half means 2 equal parts. Half of 10 is 5, because 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: Which Roman numeral means 5?
items.h: Romans wrote I for 1, V for 5, X for 10 and L for 50.

items.q: What is a shape with 8 sides called?
items.h: Octo means eight: an octopus has 8 arms and an octagon has 8 sides.

items.q: How many days are there in a fortnight?
items.h: A fortnight is 2 weeks, which is 14 days.

items.q: How many days does February have when it is not a leap year?
items.h: February has 28 days, but in a leap year it gets one more: 29.

items.q: Which month comes after March?
items.h: April is the fourth month of the year, and it has 30 days.

items.q: Which day comes after Friday?
items.h: Saturday and Sunday make the weekend.

items.q: How many centimetres are there in a metre?
items.h: A metre is 100 centimetres, and a kilometre is 1,000 metres.

items.q: How many grams are there in a kilogram?
items.h: A kilogram is 1,000 grams, about the weight of a bag of sugar.

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.h: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes, because 4 lots of 15 make 60.

items.q: Which shape has no corners at all?
items.h: A circle has no corners, which is why wheels are round and roll smoothly.

items.q: How many years are there in a millennium?
items.h: A millennium is 1,000 years, and a century is 100 years.

items.q: What do we call 10 years?
items.h: A decade is 10 years, so 10 decades make a century.
